claims.claim: An answer must contain a general or specific denial of the material allegations the defendant controverts.
claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.

claims.claim: An answer must state any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
(2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.
The defenses shall be separately stated

claims.claim: The several defenses must refer to the causes of action they are intended to answer.
claims.quote: the several defenses shall refer to the causes of action which they are intended to answer, in a manner by which they may be intelligibly distinguished.
claims.note: The reference is required, but the draft omits the standard for how it must be made.

claims.claim: A general denial is sufficient only in the situations described in Section 431.30(d).
claims.quote: However, if the cause of action is a claim assigned to a third party for collection and the complaint is verified, the denial of the allegations shall be made positively or according to the information and belief of the defendant, even if the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1.
claims.note: The cross-reference is accurate but does not identify the conditions: an unverified complaint or one subject to Article 2 generally permits a general denial, with the quoted exception for verified assigned collection claims.

claims.claim: A general denial only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.
claims.quote: a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.

claims.claim: The time limit is four years for an action on a contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: Supported within the stated unsecured-contract scope and subject to the stated exception.

claims.claim: Section 336a is an exception to the four-year rule.

flags.text: The draft omits §431.30(g)’s requirement that the references make the defenses intelligibly distinguishable.
The bare reference to §431.30(d) does not tell readers when a general denial suffices or identify the exception for a verified complaint on a claim assigned for collection.

result.summary: The four-year limit and §336a exception are supported for the stated scope. The pleading discussion omits two conditions that matter within that scope.
